claims.text: The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a homogeneous, equiaxed, single-phase solid solution.
The Co-free alloy has a microstructure similar to that of the equiatomic Co-containing baseline alloy.
Elevated temperature and a moderate strain rate induce a transition from predominantly dislocation-driven plasticity to enhanced grain-boundary sliding and migration in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Grain-boundary sliding and migration mediate a favorable strength–ductility balance relative to the Co-containing baseline alloy.
Evolving intergranular strain concentrations together with EBSD or TEM microstructural changes identify active grain-boundary sliding and migration.
Elevated temperature reduces intergranular bonding strength in the Co-free alloy.
Reduced intergranular bonding strength favors grain-boundary sliding over dislocation slip.
Grain-boundary sliding produces deformation localized along grain boundaries.
The proposed grain-boundary mechanism decreases yield stress.
The proposed grain-boundary mechanism enhances ductility.
At higher temperatures, the Co-free alloy will exhibit a greater frequency and amplitude of grain-boundary-localized strain than the Co-containing baseline.
At higher temperatures, the Co-free alloy will have a lower yield stress than the Co-containing baseline.
At higher temperatures, the Co-free alloy will have greater ductility than the Co-containing baseline.
Under comparable test conditions, the Co-containing baseline deforms predominantly by intragranular dislocation slip.
Under comparable test conditions, grain-boundary sliding makes only a minimal contribution in the Co-containing baseline.
The grain-boundary mechanism is expected to dominate above approximately 200 °C at a strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1.
Conditions outside the specified temperature and strain-rate regime may reduce the prominence of grain-boundary sliding.
Microstructural heterogeneities may alter the transition temperature and the magnitude of the grain-boundary contribution.
